items.title: The coupled quadratic oscillator model: mass metric, stiffness, generalized force, modal vocabulary and the small-oscillation model at a mechanical equilibrium
items.statement:
**(a) Data of a coupled quadratic model.** A **coupled quadratic model** (a
**quadratic oscillator model**) is declared by the following data: an integer
$n\ge1$, the number of **degrees of freedom**; a **mass metric matrix**
$M\in M_{n}(\mathbb R)$, symmetric and positive definite, that is
$M=M^{\mathsf T}$ and $v^{\mathsf T}Mv>0$ for every nonzero
$v\in\mathbb R^{n}$ ([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]],
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); a **stiffness matrix**
$K\in M_{n}(\mathbb R)$, symmetric, $K=K^{\mathsf T}$; and, when the model is
read as forced, an interval $I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]) together with a continuous **generalized force**
$J:I_{0}\to\mathbb R^{n}$ ([[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]).
The coordinates $q_{1},\dots,q_{n}$ of $\mathbb R^{n}$ are read in the chart
in which the model is declared and carry declared dimensions
$\gamma_{1},\dots,\gamma_{n}$ and units, and time is read in seconds and mass
in kilograms ([[def-cm01-units]]). The data carry the dimensions

$$[M_{ij}]=\mu\ell^{2}\gamma_{i}^{-1}\gamma_{j}^{-1},\qquad [K_{ij}]=\mu\ell^{2}\gamma_{i}^{-1}\gamma_{j}^{-1}\tau^{-2},\qquad [J_{i}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}\gamma_{i}^{-1},$$

so that $\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}Mv$, $\tfrac12q^{\mathsf T}Kq$ and the pairing
$J\cdot\delta q$ of the generalized force with a coordinate variation all have
the energy dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; if the coordinate $q_{i}$ is
length-valued, $\gamma_{i}=\ell$, the entry $J_{i}$ has the force dimension
$\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$. This is the dimension bookkeeping of a generalized
coordinate description in the sense of
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]], whose kinetic metric and
generalized forces are the framework objects the data present; the matrices
$M$ and $K$ are model parameters, not measured quantities.

**(b) Model equation, motions and phase system.** The equation of the model
with data $(M,K,J)$ is

$$M\,q''(t)+K\,q(t)=J(t)\qquad(t\in I_{0}).$$

A **motion** of the model is a curve $q:J\to\mathbb R^{n}$ of class $C^{2}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) on an interval
$J\subseteq I_{0}$ with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) satisfying the
equation for every $t\in J$. A **datum** at $t_{0}\in I_{0}$ is a pair
$(q_{0},v_{0})\in\mathbb R^{n}\times\mathbb R^{n}$. The **phase system** of
the model is the first-order linear system $z'=A z+b(t)$ on
$I_{0}\times\mathbb R^{2n}$ with $z=(q,v)$ and

$$A=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_{n}\\-M^{-1}K&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad b(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0\\M^{-1}J(t)\end{pmatrix},$$

where $M^{-1}$ is the inverse of $M$. By the product rule and invertibility of
$M$, a $C^{1}$ curve $t\mapsto(q(t),v(t))$ solves the phase system if and only
if $q$ is a motion of the model and $v=q'$. The model is **free** when
$J\equiv0$ and **forced, with generalized force $J$,** otherwise; the read of
$J$ as a prescribed external generalized force is the modelling status of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] for the external contributions
of a force model.

**(c) Quadratic energies and the mass metric.** The **kinetic energy**, the
**potential energy of the stiffness** and the **mechanical energy** of the
model are

$$T(v):=\tfrac12\,v^{\mathsf T}Mv,\qquad U_{K}(q):=\tfrac12\,q^{\mathsf T}Kq,\qquad E(q,v):=T(v)+U_{K}(q),$$

all of energy dimension. $U_{K}$ is defined for every symmetric $K$; the name
records that $K$ is the matrix through which the model enters, and when $K$ is
indefinite $U_{K}$ is not non-negative, the model is not presented by a
potential with a local minimum at the origin, and no stability vocabulary is
attached to it by this item. The quadratic form $v\mapsto v^{\mathsf T}Mv$ is
positive definite and is called the **mass metric** of the model; the word
"metric" records only this positive-definiteness, and no distance on
configuration space is defined here.

**(d) Small-oscillation model at an equilibrium.** Let a mechanical system in
a chart be given by a $C^{2}$ field $q\mapsto G_{\mathrm{kin}}(q)$ of
symmetric positive definite matrices on an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb
R^{n}$ and a $C^{2}$ potential $U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$
([[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]]), and let
$q_{0}\in\Omega$ be a **mechanical equilibrium**, $\nabla U(q_{0})=0$. Its
**small-oscillation model at $q_{0}$** is the coupled quadratic model with
degrees of freedom $n$, mass metric matrix $M:=G_{\mathrm{kin}}(q_{0})$,
**stiffness matrix** $K_{0}:=D^{2}U(q_{0})$ — the Hessian of the potential
([[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]], symmetric by
[[cor-hessian-is-symmetric]]) — and zero generalized force, read in the
displacement coordinates $\xi:=q-q_{0}$. When the chart arises from the
generalized-coordinate dictionary of
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]], the matrix
$G_{\mathrm{kin}}(q_{0})=DX(q_{0})^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q_{0})$ is the
value at $q_{0}$ of that dictionary's kinetic metric. This clause assigns
model data to the equilibrium; the identification of the assigned model with
the derivative of the mechanical field, and every statement about its motions,
are separate results and are not asserted here.

**(e) Modal vocabulary of the decoupling data.** By
[[thm-cm-quadratic-mode-decomposition]] applied to the symmetric positive
definite $M$ and the symmetric matrix $K$ there are a symmetric positive
definite square root $M^{1/2}$, its inverse $M^{-1/2}$, an orthogonal matrix
$O$ with $O^{\mathsf T}=O^{-1}$, and a diagonal matrix
$\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n})$ with
$M^{-1/2}KM^{-1/2}=O\Lambda O^{\mathsf T}$. The **modal coordinates** of the
model are $z:=O^{\mathsf T}M^{1/2}q$, a linear bijection of $\mathbb R^{n}$,
and the **modal vectors** are the columns $u_{i}:=M^{-1/2}Oe_{i}$; the numbers
$\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n}$ are the **modal stiffnesses**. The identities
$Ku_{i}=\lambda_{i}Mu_{i}$ and $u_{i}^{\mathsf T}Mu_{j}=\delta_{ij}$ are part
of the modal theorem and are used by name on this page. An index $i$ (or the
mode it labels) is **oscillatory** when $\lambda_{i}>0$, with **mode
frequency** $\omega_{i}:=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}>0$ (the nonnegative square root;
dimension $\tau^{-1}$, read in radians per second under the angle convention
of [[def-cm01-units]]); it is a **zero mode** when $\lambda_{i}=0$; and it is
an **unstable (exponential) direction** when $\lambda_{i}<0$. Two distinct
indices $i\ne j$ are **degenerate** when $\lambda_{i}=\lambda_{j}$; for a real
number $\lambda$ the set $E_{\lambda}:=\{u\in\mathbb R^{n}:(K-\lambda M)u=0\}$
is the **modal eigenspace** of $\lambda$, a linear subspace whose dimension is
the number of indices with $\lambda_{i}=\lambda$. The model is **oscillatory**
when $K$ is non-negative, $q^{\mathsf T}Kq\ge0$ for all $q$; then every modal
stiffness is $\ge0$, the zero modes are the indices with $\lambda_{i}=0$, and
the eigenvalue $0$ has multiplicity $\dim\ker K$.

**(f) Status.** This item introduces objects, vocabulary, domains, regularity
and dimensions for the restricted model class of this page and assigns its
small-oscillation model to a mechanical equilibrium. It contains no
existence, uniqueness, conservation, stability, resonance, degeneracy or
approximation assertion; those are proved on this page as separate items. It
adopts no force law of nature and records no measured value. Every later
statement of this page names the data $(M,K,J)$ or the mechanical data
$(G_{\mathrm{kin}},U,q_{0})$ it uses, and the one-dimensional instance is
recorded in the remarks.
items.strategy: Define the quadratic model class: mass metric, stiffness, prescribed generalized force, quadratic energies, the phase system, the modal vocabulary of the decoupling transform and the small-oscillation model assigned to a mechanical equilibrium; assert nothing beyond the definitions and the recorded dimension bookkeeping.
items.physical_scope: The restricted model class used on this page: a constant mass metric matrix M (symmetric positive definite) and a constant symmetric stiffness matrix K in a chart of n coordinate directions, with an optional prescribed generalized force J(t), and the model equation M q'' + K q = J(t); together with the quadratic kinetic and potential energies, the phase system, the modal vocabulary of the decoupling transform, and the small-oscillation model assigned to a mechanical equilibrium q_0 of a chart mechanical system, whose mass metric is M(q_0) and whose stiffness is the potential Hessian D^2 U(q_0). The item declares vocabulary, domains, regularity and dimensions only; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, conservation, stability, resonance or approximation statement, adopts no force law of nature, records no measured value, and states no empirical applicability. In particular the mass metric and the stiffness are model parameters of the declared chart, not measured quantities, and the quadratic model is an idealization whose accuracy near an equilibrium is quantified only by the approximation theorems of this page.

items.title: The free coupled quadratic model: global existence, the complete modal classification, mode energies, intrinsic degenerate mode subspaces, boundedness and the unstable direction
items.statement:
Global-time, growth and boundedness claims below refer to the unique maximal extension of the autonomous free equation on $\mathbb R$; local motions remain its restrictions. Values at $0$ in coefficient formulas are evaluated on that extension when the original interval omits $0$.

Adopt the free coupled quadratic model of
[[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with data $(M,K,J)$ in which
$J\equiv0$, $M$ is symmetric positive definite and $K$ is symmetric, with
modal data $M^{1/2}$, $M^{-1/2}$, $O$, $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n})$,
modal coordinates $z=O^{\mathsf T}M^{1/2}q$ and mode frequencies
$\omega_{i}=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}$ for $\lambda_{i}>0$. Write
$\kappa_{i}:=\sqrt{-\lambda_{i}}$ for $\lambda_{i}<0$. Then:

1. **Existence and uniqueness on the whole line.** For every $t_{0}\in\mathbb R$
and every datum $(q_{0},v_{0})\in\mathbb R^{2n}$ there is exactly one motion
$q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^{n}$ with $q(t_{0})=q_{0}$ and $q'(t_{0})=v_{0}$; it
is the unique maximal motion through that datum.
2. **Complete modal classification.** A curve $q:J\to\mathbb R^{n}$ of class
$C^{2}$ on an interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior is a
motion of the free model if and only if its modal coordinates satisfy

$$z_{i}(t)=a_{i}\cos(\omega_{i}t)+b_{i}\sin(\omega_{i}t)\ (\lambda_{i}>0),\qquad z_{i}(t)=a_{i}+b_{i}t\ (\lambda_{i}=0),\qquad z_{i}(t)=a_{i}\cosh(\kappa_{i}t)+b_{i}\sinh(\kappa_{i}t)\ (\lambda_{i}<0)$$

for real numbers $a_{i},b_{i}$; the coefficients are unique and are
determined by the datum of the unique maximal extension through $a_{i}=z_{i}(0)$, $b_{i}=z_{i}'(0)/\omega_{i}$
for $\lambda_{i}>0$, $b_{i}=z_{i}'(0)$ for $\lambda_{i}=0$ and
$b_{i}=z_{i}'(0)/\kappa_{i}$ for $\lambda_{i}<0$.
3. **Energy and mode energies.** Along every motion the mechanical energy is
constant, and with $E_{i}:=\tfrac12\bigl(z_{i}'^{2}+\lambda_{i}z_{i}^{2}\bigr)$
one has $E(q,q')=\sum_{i=1}^{n}E_{i}$ and every $E_{i}$ is constant; for the
families of clause 2,

$$E_{i}=\tfrac12\omega_{i}^{2}\bigl(a_{i}^{2}+b_{i}^{2}\bigr)\ (\lambda_{i}>0),\qquad E_{i}=\tfrac12b_{i}^{2}\ (\lambda_{i}=0),\qquad E_{i}=\tfrac12\kappa_{i}^{2}\bigl(b_{i}^{2}-a_{i}^{2}\bigr)\ (\lambda_{i}<0).$$

4. **Degenerate families are intrinsic.** Let $\lambda$ be a modal stiffness,
let $E_{\lambda}^{S}:=\{u\in\mathbb R^{n}:M^{-1/2}KM^{-1/2}u=\lambda u\}$ and
let $N_{\lambda}:=M^{-1/2}E_{\lambda}^{S}$, a subspace of dimension equal to
the multiplicity of $\lambda$. A motion $q$ satisfies $z_{i}\equiv0$ for every
index $i$ with $\lambda_{i}\ne\lambda$ if and only if $q$ is a $C^{2}$ curve
with $q(t)\in N_{\lambda}$ for all $t$ in its interval and $q''+\lambda q=0$.
Consequently the family of such **pure-$\lambda$ motions** is independent of
the choice of diagonalization $O$: for $\lambda>0$ it consists exactly of
$q(t)=\cos(\omega t)q_{0}+\omega^{-1}\sin(\omega t)q_{1}$ with
$q_{0},q_{1}\in N_{\lambda}$ and $\omega=\sqrt{\lambda}$, for $\lambda=0$ of
$q(t)=q_{0}+tq_{1}$ with $q_{0},q_{1}\in N_{\lambda}$, and for $\lambda<0$ of
$q(t)=\cosh(\kappa t)q_{0}+\kappa^{-1}\sinh(\kappa t)q_{1}$ with
$\kappa=\sqrt{-\lambda}$. These formulas on a local interval are restrictions of their unique maximal extensions; $q_0,q_1$ are the position and velocity of that extension at time $0$, even if the local interval omits $0$. The individual modal vectors $u_{i}$ are not
intrinsic when the multiplicity exceeds one.
5. **Boundedness.** If $K$ is positive definite then every motion is bounded
on $\mathbb R$. If $K$ is non-negative and some $\lambda_{i}=0$, then a
motion with $z_{i}'\equiv b_{i}\ne0$ on a zero mode is unbounded on
$[0,\infty)$: the zero mode is affine, not oscillatory.
6. **Unstable direction.** If $K$ is not non-negative, then $(0,0)$ is not a
Lyapunov stable rest point of the free model
([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]): there is $\varepsilon_{0}>0$
such that for every $\delta>0$ there are data with
$\lVert(q_{0},v_{0})\rVert_{2}<\delta$ whose motion reaches
$\lVert(q(t),q'(t))\rVert_{2}=\varepsilon_{0}$ at some time $t>0$.

The statement is read for the declared model data; no value of any parameter,
no physical realization and no measured frequency is asserted.
items.strategy: Cases: transport the free system through the modal bijection, solve the three scalar families, read the energy decomposition and boundedness, characterize degenerate pure-lambda families intrinsically, and exhibit the exponential escaping family of a negative modal stiffness.
items.physical_scope: The free coupled quadratic model M q'' + K q = 0 of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with symmetric positive definite mass metric M and symmetric stiffness K: existence and uniqueness of motions for every datum on the whole real line, the complete classification of motions into oscillatory, affine and exponential modal families with mode frequencies sqrt(lambda_i), the conservation of the mechanical energy with the modal energy decomposition, the intrinsic (basis-free) description of degenerate pure-lambda families in the subspace ker(K - lambda M), boundedness of every motion when K is positive definite, unbounded growth of the affine zero-mode motions and of the exponential directions, and the Lyapunov instability of the rest point of the free model when K has a negative modal stiffness. The result is a conditional statement about the declared model class; it contains no claim that any physical system is described by it, no measured stiffness, mass or frequency, and no empirical qualification beyond the exact idealization of the model.

items.title: Small oscillations at a strict minimum: the linearized model, its normal modes and the Lyapunov stability of the nonlinear equilibrium
items.statement:
Adopt the mechanical system in a chart of
[[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]] with kinetic metric
field $M:\Omega\to M_{n}(\mathbb R)$ of class $C^{2}$, symmetric positive
definite at every point of the open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$, and
potential $U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$; write $G$ for its
mechanical vector field on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{n}$. Let $q_{0}\in\Omega$
be a **strict local minimum** of $U$: $\nabla U(q_{0})=0$ and there is
$r_{0}>0$ with $\overline B(q_{0},r_{0})\subseteq\Omega$ and
$U(q)>U(q_{0})$ for $0<\lVert q-q_{0}\rVert_{2}<r_{0}$. Let
$M_{0}:=M(q_{0})$ and $K:=D^{2}U(q_{0})$. Then:

1. $K$ is symmetric and non-negative, and the small-oscillation model at
$q_{0}$ of clause (d) of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] — the coupled
quadratic model with mass metric matrix $M_{0}$, stiffness $K$ and zero
generalized force, in the displacement coordinates $\xi=q-q_{0}$ — is an
oscillatory model in the sense of clause (e) of that definition;
2. the linearization of $G$ at $(q_{0},0)$ is
$$DG(q_{0},0)(\delta q,\delta v)=\bigl(\delta v,\,-M_{0}^{-1}K\,\delta q\bigr)\qquad(\delta q,\delta v\in\mathbb R^{n}),$$
and for a curve $\xi:J\to\mathbb R^{n}$ of class $C^{2}$ on an interval $J$
with nonempty interior the following are equivalent: $\xi$ is a motion of the
small-oscillation model, $M_{0}\xi''+K\xi=0$ on $J$, and $t\mapsto(\xi(t),\xi'(t))$
solves the linear system $y'=DG(q_{0},0)y$ on $J$;
3. the motions of the small-oscillation model are exactly the modal
superpositions of clause 2 of [[pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy]] with
every modal stiffness $\lambda_{i}\ge0$: there are no exponential
pure-$\lambda$ families, every oscillatory frequency is
$\omega_{i}=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}$, and the pure-$\lambda$ motions of a
degenerate stiffness are the solutions of $q''+\lambda q=0$ with values in
the intrinsic subspace $N_{\lambda}=M_{0}^{-1/2}\{u:M_{0}^{-1/2}KM_{0}^{-1/2}u=\lambda u\}$;
4. $(q_{0},0)$ is a Lyapunov stable equilibrium of the nonlinear mechanical
system: for every $\varepsilon>0$ with
$\overline B((q_{0},0),\varepsilon)\subseteq\Omega\times\mathbb R^{n}$ there
is $\delta>0$ such that every maximal solution of $z'=G(z)$ with
$\lVert z(0)-(q_{0},0)\rVert_{2}<\delta$ exists for all $t\ge0$ and stays
within distance $\varepsilon$ of $(q_{0},0)$.

No asymptotic attraction, no all-time validity of the linear model as an
approximation of the nonlinear motion, and no measured frequency is asserted.
items.strategy: Direct: assemble the assigned small-oscillation model from the definition, identify the derivative linearization with the model phase system, read the non-negative normal-mode classification, and invoke the energy-stability theorem for the nonlinear statement.
items.physical_scope: A mechanical system in a chart at a strict local minimum of its potential: the assigned small-oscillation quadratic model with mass metric M(q_0) and stiffness the Hessian D^2 U(q_0) (symmetric and non-negative), the identification of that model with the derivative linearization of the mechanical field, the complete normal-mode classification of the linearized motions with frequencies sqrt(lambda_i) and no exponential directions, and the Lyapunov stability of the nonlinear equilibrium by exact energy conservation. The stability conclusion is a statement about the declared chart model; it asserts no asymptotic attraction, no measured frequency, no particular physical system and no empirical claim, and the accuracy of the linear model as an approximation of the nonlinear motion is a separate finite-time statement on this page.

items.title: Finite-time error control for the small-oscillation approximation: the quadratic remainder of the mechanical field and the variation-of-constants bound
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ be open, let
$M:\Omega\to M_{n}(\mathbb R)$ be a field of class $C^{3}$ with $M(q)$
symmetric positive definite for every $q\in\Omega$, and let
$U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{3}$ with $\nabla U(q_{0})=0$ at a point
$q_{0}\in\Omega$. Let $G$ be the mechanical vector field of
[[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]] on
$\Omega\times\mathbb R^{n}$, let $r_{0}>0$ satisfy
$\overline B(q_{0},r_{0})\subseteq\Omega$ and define
$F:\{\zeta=(\delta q,\delta v):q_{0}+\delta q\in\Omega\}\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ by
$F(\delta q,\delta v):=G(q_{0}+\delta q,\delta v)$. Put
$A:=DF(0)=DG(q_{0},0)$. Then:

1. $F$ is of class $C^{2}$, $F(0)=0$, $F$ is locally Lipschitz in the state
variable, and
$$DG(q_{0},0)(\delta q,\delta v)=\bigl(\delta v,\,-M(q_{0})^{-1}D^{2}U(q_{0})\,\delta q\bigr);$$
moreover there are constants $C,L\ge0$ with
$$\lVert F(\zeta)-A\zeta\rVert_{2}\le C\lVert\zeta\rVert_{2}^{2},\qquad \lVert F(\zeta)\rVert_{2}\le L\lVert\zeta\rVert_{2}\qquad(\lVert\zeta\rVert_{2}\le r_{0});$$
one may take $L=\sup_{\lVert\eta\rVert_{2}\le r_{0}}\lVert DF(\eta)\rVert$
([[def-operator-norm]]) and $C=\Lambda/2$ for any Lipschitz constant
$\Lambda$ of $DF$ on the closed ball
$\overline B(0,r_{0})\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ ([[def-metric-ball]]).
2. For every datum $z_{0}=(q_{0}+\delta q_{0},v_{0})$ with
$\delta:=\lVert(\delta q_{0},v_{0})\rVert_{2}>0$ and every $T>0$ with
$\delta e^{LT}<r_{0}$, the maximal solution $z=(q,v)$ of $z'=G(z)$ with
$z(0)=z_{0}$ is defined on $[0,T]$ ([[def-maximal-ode-solution]]) and
satisfies, for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\lVert z(t)-y(t)\rVert_{2}\le C\delta^{2}\,t\,e^{(\lVert A\rVert+2L)t},$$
where $y(t)=(q_0+\xi(t),\eta(t))$ and $\widetilde y=(\xi,\eta):\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ solves $\widetilde y'=A\widetilde y$, $\widetilde y(0)=(\delta q_0,v_0)$. Thus $y$ is the linear approximation translated back to the original chart.
3. Writing $\widetilde y=(\xi,\eta)$ for the displacement linear solution of clause 2, the first
component $\xi$ is exactly the unique motion of the small-oscillation model
at $q_{0}$ of clause (d) of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with datum
$(\delta q_{0},v_{0})$: $\xi$ is $C^{2}$ on $\mathbb R$ with
$M(q_{0})\xi''+D^{2}U(q_{0})\xi=0$, $\xi(0)=\delta q_{0}$ and
$\xi'(0)=v_{0}$.

No all-time statement, no statement for data violating the smallness
condition $\delta e^{LT}<r_{0}$, and no value of any measured quantity is
asserted.
items.strategy: Direct: prove the quadratic-remainder bounds for the translated mechanical field by compactness and the fundamental theorem along rays, then apply the finite-time linearization theorem and identify the linear solution with the small-oscillation motion.
items.physical_scope: Finite-time error control for the small-oscillation model of a mechanical system in a chart at a mechanical equilibrium: for a C^3 kinetic metric field and a C^3 potential with vanishing gradient at q_0, the mechanical field is C^2 near the equilibrium, its Taylor remainder at the linearization is quadratic with constants obtained from compactness, and the finite-time variation-of-constants estimate bounds the difference between the nonlinear motion and the linearized (normal-mode) motion by C delta^2 t exp((||A||+2L)t) on every horizon T with delta exp(LT)<r_0. The statement is a conditional finite-time estimate for the declared chart model under explicit regularity and smallness hypotheses; it asserts no all-time validity of the linear approximation, no stability conclusion, no large-data statement and no empirical claim, and the constants depend on the model data only through its behaviour on the stated ball.

items.title: The forced coupled quadratic model: decoupled modal responses, sinusoidal drive, resonance at the modal frequencies and boundedness away from resonance
items.statement:
Adopt the coupled quadratic model of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with
data $(M,K,J)$ in which $M$ is symmetric positive definite, $K$ is symmetric
and non-negative, $I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an interval with nonempty
interior and $J:I_{0}\to\mathbb R^{n}$ is continuous; let
$O,\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n})$,
$\omega_{i}=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}$ for $\lambda_{i}>0$ and the modal coordinates
$z=O^{\mathsf T}M^{1/2}q$ be the modal data of clause (e) of that definition,
and call $\psi:=O^{\mathsf T}M^{-1/2}J$ the **modal force**. Fix
$t_{0}\in I_{0}$ and a datum $(q_{0},v_{0})$, and write
$\xi_{i}:=z_{i}(t_{0})$, $\eta_{i}:=z_{i}'(t_{0})$ for the modal data of the
motion. Then:

1. **Unique motion and modal convolution.** There is exactly one motion
$q:I_{0}\to\mathbb R^{n}$ with that datum; it is $q=M^{-1/2}Oz$ with

$$z_{i}(t)=\xi_{i}\cos\bigl(\omega_{i}(t-t_{0})\bigr)+\frac{\eta_{i}}{\omega_{i}}\sin\bigl(\omega_{i}(t-t_{0})\bigr)+\frac{1}{\omega_{i}}\int_{t_{0}}^{t}\sin\bigl(\omega_{i}(t-s)\bigr)\psi_{i}(s)\,ds\quad(\lambda_{i}>0),$$

$$z_{i}(t)=\xi_{i}+\eta_{i}(t-t_{0})+\int_{t_{0}}^{t}(t-s)\psi_{i}(s)\,ds\quad(\lambda_{i}=0).$$

2. **Sinusoidal generalized force.** Suppose $I_{0}=\mathbb R$ and
$J(t)=J_{0}\cos(\Omega t)$ with $J_{0}\in\mathbb R^{n}$ and $\Omega\ge0$, so
that $\psi(t)=\psi_{0}\cos(\Omega t)$ with
$\psi_{0}=O^{\mathsf T}M^{-1/2}J_{0}$. Then for each index $i$:
   (a) if $\lambda_{i}>0$ and $\Omega^{2}\ne\lambda_{i}$, then
   $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}(t):=\psi_{0,i}\cos(\Omega t)/(\lambda_{i}-\Omega^{2})$
   solves $z_{i}''+\lambda_{i}z_{i}=\psi_{0,i}\cos(\Omega t)$ on $\mathbb R$,
   with amplitude $|\psi_{0,i}|/|\lambda_{i}-\Omega^{2}|$;
   (b) if $\lambda_{i}>0$ and $\Omega^{2}=\lambda_{i}$, then
   $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}(t):=\psi_{0,i}\,t\sin(\omega_{i}t)/(2\omega_{i})$
   solves that equation and is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$ when
   $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$;
   (c) if $\lambda_{i}=0$ and $\Omega>0$, then
   $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}(t):=-\psi_{0,i}\cos(\Omega t)/\Omega^{2}$ solves
   $z_{i}''=\psi_{0,i}\cos(\Omega t)$ and is bounded; if $\lambda_{i}=0$ and
   $\Omega=0$, then $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}(t):=\psi_{0,i}t^{2}/2$ solves
   $z_{i}''=\psi_{0,i}$ and is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$ when
   $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$.
3. **Reduction, resonance and boundedness.** In every case of clause 2 the
modal particular functions $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}$ combine into the particular
motion $q^{\mathrm{p}}:=M^{-1/2}Oz^{\mathrm{p}}$ of the model, and every
motion of the model on $\mathbb R$ is $q=q^{\mathrm{p}}+q^{\mathrm{h}}$ with
$q^{\mathrm{h}}$ a motion of the free model of
[[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]]. Consequently:
   (a) **resonance.** If some index $i$ has $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$ and either
   $\lambda_{i}>0$ with $\Omega^{2}=\lambda_{i}$, or $\lambda_{i}=0$ with
   $\Omega=0$, then every motion of the model is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$;
   (b) **boundedness.** If $K$ is positive definite and no index $i$ with
   $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$ satisfies $\Omega^{2}=\lambda_{i}$, then every motion of
   the model is bounded on $[0,\infty)$.
   The resonant drive angular frequencies are exactly the values
   $\Omega=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}$ with $\lambda_{i}>0$ and $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$,
   together with $\Omega=0$ when some index with $\lambda_{i}=0$ has
   $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$.

The generalized force is prescribed external data in the modelling status of
[[post-cm04-sinusoidal-drive-model]]: it is a function of time alone, the
source is not modelled dynamically, and no back-reaction, damping, measured
response or empirical value is asserted.

items.title: Averaging for a weakly damped oscillator: the rotating-frame amplitude, the averaged exponential energy decay and the order-$\varepsilon$ bound on the $O(1/\varepsilon)$ time scale
items.statement:
Adopt the strictly damped oscillator model of
[[post-cm04-linear-damping-model]] with fixed data $m>0$, $k>0$ and drag
coefficient $c=\varepsilon\gamma$, where $\varepsilon>0$ and $\gamma>0$ are
given; its equation is

$$m\,x''(t)+\varepsilon\gamma\,x'(t)+k\,x(t)=0 .$$

Put $\omega_{0}:=\sqrt{k/m}$ and identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^{2}$.
For a motion $x$ define the **rotating-frame amplitude**

$$\zeta(t):=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\omega_{0}}}\bigl(\omega_{0}x(t)+i\,x'(t)\bigr)e^{i\omega_{0}t}\in\mathbb C,$$

and define $F:\mathbb R\times\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ by

$$F(t,\zeta):=-\frac{i\gamma}{m}\,e^{i\omega_{0}t}\bigl(\cos(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Im}\zeta-\sin(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Re}\zeta\bigr).$$

Then:

1. **Global motions and the slow system.** Every datum
$(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})\in\mathbb R^{3}$ has exactly one maximal motion, and it
is defined on all of $\mathbb R$. The map $x\mapsto\zeta$ is a bijection
from the motions $x:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of the model onto the solutions
$\zeta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ of the first-order system
$\zeta'=\varepsilon F(t,\zeta)$, with inverse
$\zeta\mapsto x(t)=\sqrt{2/\omega_{0}}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e^{-i\omega_{0}t}\zeta(t)\bigr)$.
2. **Averaging data.** $F$ is of class $C^{\infty}$ on
$\mathbb R\times\mathbb C$, is $P$-periodic in $t$ with $P:=2\pi/\omega_{0}$,
and its average in the sense of
[[def-cm-averaging-data-and-averaged-field]] is
$\bar F(\zeta)=-\gamma\zeta/(2m)$; the averaged system is
$\zeta'=-\varepsilon\gamma\zeta/(2m)$, with the global solution
$\bar\zeta(t)=\zeta_{0}e^{-\varepsilon\gamma t/(2m)}$ for the datum
$\zeta_{0}=\zeta(0)$.
3. **Order-$\varepsilon$ estimate on the $O(1/\varepsilon)$ time scale.**
Let $\zeta_{0}\in\mathbb C$ with $\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert>0$, let
$0<\rho<R$ be real numbers and put
$$M:=\frac{\gamma}{m}\sqrt2\,\bigl(\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert+R\bigr),\qquad L:=\frac{\gamma}{m}\sqrt2,\qquad B:=2MP,\qquad B_{1}:=2LP,$$
$$K:=e^{LA}\bigl[B+(LB+B_{1}M)A\bigr]$$
for a parameter $A>0$. Suppose $\varepsilon K<\rho$ and suppose the averaged
solution satisfies $\lVert\bar\zeta(t)-\zeta_{0}\rVert_{2}\le R-\rho$ for
every $t\in[0,A/\varepsilon]$; this holds whenever
$\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert>R-\rho$ and
$\gamma A/(2m)\le\ln\bigl(\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert/(\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert-(R-\rho))\bigr)$.
Then the solution $\zeta$ of $\zeta'=\varepsilon F(t,\zeta)$ with
$\zeta(0)=\zeta_{0}$ exists on $[0,A/\varepsilon]$ and satisfies
$$\lVert\zeta(t)-\bar\zeta(t)\rVert_{2}\le\varepsilon K\qquad(0\le t\le A/\varepsilon).$$
4. **Energy reading.** For every motion the mechanical energy satisfies
$$E(t):=\tfrac12m\,x'(t)^{2}+\tfrac12k\,x(t)^{2}=m\omega_{0}\lvert\zeta(t)\rvert^{2},$$
so with $E_{0}:=E(0)=m\omega_{0}\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert^{2}$ the estimate of
clause 3 gives
$$\bigl\lvert E(t)-E_{0}e^{-\varepsilon\gamma t/m}\bigr\rvert\le m\omega_{0}\,\varepsilon K\bigl(2\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert+\varepsilon K\bigr)\qquad(0\le t\le A/\varepsilon).$$

The averaged system is a different model from the exact one, and the
statements are conditional on the displayed smallness and trapping
hypotheses; no exact decay law, no measured decay rate, and no empirical
claim is asserted.

items.physical_scope: The strictly damped one-dimensional oscillator model m x'' + epsilon gamma x' + k x = 0 with m>0, k>0, small parameter epsilon>0 and fixed gamma>0: the exact rotating-frame amplitude zeta(t) = (omega_0 x + i x') exp(i omega_0 t)/sqrt(2 omega_0) and its slow equation zeta' = epsilon F(t,zeta) with F smooth and periodic in time, the averaged equation zeta' = -(epsilon gamma/(2m)) zeta with the exponential averaged solution, the order-epsilon averaging estimate on the O(1/epsilon) time scale under the stated smallness, trapping and constant hypotheses, and the resulting exponential energy-decay estimate |E(t) - E_0 exp(-epsilon gamma t/m)| <= m omega_0 epsilon K (2|zeta_0|+epsilon K). The result is a conditional finite-time statement about the declared damped model; the averaged system is a different model compared with the exact one, no exact energy decay law is asserted, no measured decay rate or quality factor is reported and no empirical claim is made.

items.title: Scope of the coupled quadratic model: zero modes, degenerate eigenspaces, unstable quadratic directions and the limits of the approximation statements
items.statement:
A **zero mode** of a coupled quadratic model is an index with modal
stiffness $\lambda_{i}=0$ ([[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] clause (e));
the multiplicity of the value $0$ is $\dim\ker K$, and it counts the
independent directions in which the quadratic model exerts no restoring
force. By clause 2 of [[pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy]] the free motion
in such a direction is affine, $z_{i}(t)=a_{i}+b_{i}t$, not oscillatory; for
$b_{i}\ne0$ it is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$. The classical instance is the
translation mode of a chain or molecule: the linearisation of a
translation-invariant model at a non-isolated minimum has a flat
second-order direction, and the "mode" of zero frequency is the uniform
motion of the whole system rather than a vibration. A constant generalized
force component along a zero mode produces quadratic growth in time by
clause 2(c) of [[pthm-cm09-forced-modal-response]], the degenerate analogue
of resonance; the model has no bounded steady response in that direction.
Zero modes are therefore excluded whenever a statement about oscillations
alone is intended: at a strict local minimum the stiffness is positive
semidefinite with $\ker K$ possibly nontrivial only if the minimum is not
isolated along those directions, and the Lyapunov stability of
[[pthm-cm09-linearization-at-a-strict-minimum]] remains valid in that case
because it does not use positivity of the stiffness.

## Degenerate modal stiffnesses

If a modal stiffness $\lambda$ has multiplicity $m>1$, the individual
eigenvectors and hence the individual modal vectors $u_{i}$ of a chosen
diagonalisation are **not** intrinsic: every orthonormal basis of the
eigenspace gives an equally valid decoupling. What is intrinsic is the
subspace $N_{\lambda}$ and its pure-$\lambda$ family of motions, exactly as
clause 4 of [[pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy]] records: the pure-$\lambda$
motions are the solutions of $q''+\lambda q=0$ with values in
$N_{\lambda}$, a family with $2m$ parameters, and for $\lambda>0$ all of them
oscillate with the single frequency $\omega=\sqrt{\lambda}$. A statement
about "the $i$-th mode" must therefore be read as a statement about a chosen
basis vector, while the frequency, the subspace and the multi-parameter
family are the basis-independent objects. Resonance of a degenerate family
with a prescribed sinusoidal force is likewise basis-independent: it occurs
exactly when the modal force vanishes in no direction of $N_{\lambda}$
(clause 2 and the remarks of [[pthm-cm09-forced-modal-response]]).

## Unstable quadratic directions

An **unstable (exponential) direction** is an index with $\lambda_{i}<0$
([[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] clause (e)). Its free motion is the
hyperbolic family $a\cosh(\kappa t)+b\sinh(\kappa t)$ with
$\kappa=\sqrt{-\lambda_{i}}$, which grows exponentially whenever it is not
identically zero, and clause 6 of [[pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy]]
proves accordingly that the rest point of the free quadratic model is not
Lyapunov stable ([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]). For a
mechanical system in a chart at a **critical** point $q_{0}$ of the potential
that is not a minimum — for instance a symmetric saddle or a strict maximum —
the stiffness $K=D^{2}U(q_{0})$ may have negative eigenvalues
([[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]]), and the corresponding
exponential directions of the linearised model exhibit the local saddle
behaviour. The linear calculation by itself certifies nothing about the
nonlinear system: the nonlinear instability of $(q_{0},0)$ follows from
[[thm-cm-instability-of-a-hyperbolic-saddle]] only when the derivative
$DG(q_{0},0)$ of the mechanical field
([[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]]) is **hyperbolic**
— no eigenvalue on the imaginary axis, in particular no zero mode — and has
an eigenvalue with positive real part. When a zero mode is present the
linearisation is not hyperbolic and the exponential-mode argument does not
apply; a higher-order analysis is then required and is not supplied here.
Conversely, a negative eigenvalue of the stiffness is necessary but not
sufficient for a physical instability statement, because the nonlinear terms
may dominate in ways the quadratic model does not see.

## Limits of the approximation statements

Three separate qualifications belong to the results of this page.

- **The quadratic model is exact only for quadratic data.** The model
$Mq''+Kq=J$ is a declared model class; it coincides with a mechanical chart
system $G_{\mathrm{kin}}(q)q''+\cdots=-\nabla U(q)$ only when the kinetic
metric is constant and the potential is quadratic. The small-oscillation
model at an equilibrium is a first-order Taylor model, and
[[pthm-cm09-linearization-at-a-strict-minimum]] identifies it with the
derivative linearization without asserting that it approximates the
nonlinear motion.

- **The linearization error bound is finite-time and small-data.** The
estimate of [[pthm-cm09-linearization-error-bound]],
$\lVert z(t)-y(t)\rVert_{2}\le C\delta^{2}te^{(\lVert A\rVert+2L)t}$ on
$[0,T]$ under $\delta e^{LT}<r_{0}$, controls the discrepancy of the
nonlinear and linear motions only for the stated horizon, datum size and
regularity; the exponential factor grows with $T$, and no all-time
closeness, stability or instability conclusion follows from it.

- **The averaging estimate is a comparison, not an identity.** The
order-$\varepsilon$ bound of [[pthm-cm09-averaging-for-weak-damping]] holds
on the $O(1/\varepsilon)$ horizon under the displayed smallness, trapping and
constant hypotheses, and compares the exact weakly damped model with a
different, averaged model; it is not an exact decay law of the damped
oscillator, and its constants $M,L,K$ depend on the chosen ball and horizon.

Beyond the mathematical qualifications, the parameters of the models of this
page — masses, stiffnesses, damping coefficients, drive amplitudes and
frequencies — are model data. A value of such a parameter taken from a
calibration experiment is an empirical premise carrying the apparatus
conditions and the measurement uncertainty, and no claim of this page
identifies a model frequency with an observed spectral line without a
specified measurement model, which is not supplied here.

items.title: Two coupled masses on a line: the in-phase and anti-phase normal modes, their frequencies, mode-energies and the zero-stiffness translation mode
items.statement:
Global-time, growth and boundedness claims below refer to the unique maximal extension of the autonomous free equation on $\mathbb R$; local motions remain its restrictions. Values at $0$ in coefficient formulas are evaluated on that extension when the original interval omits $0$.

Consider two particle labels of equal mass $m>0$ constrained to a line, with
coordinates $x_{1},x_{2}$ in metres read in a fixed inertial frame
([[def-cm01-units]]). Each label is attached to a fixed point by a spring of
stiffness $k>0$ and the labels are coupled to each other by a spring of
stiffness $c>0$; both constants are read in kilograms per second squared.
The model is the coupled quadratic model of
[[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with $n=2$, coordinates $q=(x_{1},x_{2})$,
mass metric matrix $M=mI_{2}$ and stiffness

$$K=\begin{pmatrix}k+c&-c\\-c&k+c\end{pmatrix},$$

so that the equation $Mq''+Kq=0$ is the linear chain
$m x_{1}''=-(k+c)x_{1}+cx_{2}$, $m x_{2}''=cx_{1}-(k+c)x_{2}$. Then:

1. the vectors $u_{\pm}:=(1,\pm1)/\sqrt{2m}$ satisfy
$u_{+}^{\mathsf T}Mu_{+}=u_{-}^{\mathsf T}Mu_{-}=1$,
$u_{+}^{\mathsf T}Mu_{-}=0$ and $Ku_{\pm}=\lambda_{\pm}Mu_{\pm}$ with
$$\lambda_{+}=\frac{k}{m},\qquad \lambda_{-}=\frac{k+2c}{m};$$
2. the modal coordinates are $z_{\pm}=e_{\pm}^{\mathsf T}M^{1/2}q$ with
$e_{\pm}=(1,\pm1)/\sqrt2$, that is $z_{+}=\sqrt{m/2}\,(x_{1}+x_{2})$ and
$z_{-}=\sqrt{m/2}\,(x_{1}-x_{2})$, and every motion is
$$q(t)=\bigl(A\cos(\omega_{+}t)+B\sin(\omega_{+}t)\bigr)u_{+}+\bigl(C\cos(\omega_{-}t)+D\sin(\omega_{-}t)\bigr)u_{-}$$
with $\omega_{+}=\sqrt{k/m}$ and $\omega_{-}=\sqrt{(k+2c)/m}$;
3. the initial data $q(0)=u_{+}$, $q'(0)=0$ excite exactly the in-phase mode
$q(t)=\cos(\omega_{+}t)u_{+}$, whose mechanical energy is the constant
$E=k/(2m)$; the data $q(0)=u_{-}$, $q'(0)=0$ excite exactly the anti-phase
mode $q(t)=\cos(\omega_{-}t)u_{-}$, with $E=(k+2c)/(2m)$;
4. the in-phase frequency $\omega_{+}$ is independent of the coupling $c$
and the anti-phase frequency $\omega_{-}$ is strictly increasing in $c$;
5. if $k=0$ while $c>0$, then $\lambda_{+}=0$ and $u_{+}$ spans a zero mode:
the general motion is $q(t)=(A+Bt)u_{+}+(C\cos(\omega_{-}t)+D\sin(\omega_{-}t))u_{-}$,
the pair translates freely as a whole and only the relative coordinate
oscillates, at frequency $\sqrt{2c/m}$.

items.title: A linear triatomic chain: the translation zero mode, the antisymmetric stretch and the symmetric stretch, with the corrected frequency comparison
items.statement:
Global-time, growth and boundedness claims below refer to the unique maximal extension of the autonomous free equation on $\mathbb R$; local motions remain its restrictions. Values at $0$ in coefficient formulas are evaluated on that extension when the original interval omits $0$.

Consider three particle labels constrained to a line, with coordinates
$x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ in metres and masses $m,M,m>0$ read in kilograms
([[def-cm01-units]]); the outer labels have mass $m$ and the middle label
mass $M$. Adjacent labels interact through identical springs of stiffness
$k>0$ in kilograms per second squared, and the potential is approximated by
its quadratic part $U=\tfrac{k}{2}\bigl((x_{1}-x_{2})^{2}+(x_{2}-x_{3})^{2}\bigr)$
about the equilibrium. The model is the coupled quadratic model of
[[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with $n=3$, $q=(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})$,

$$M=\operatorname{diag}(m,M,m),\qquad K=k\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&0\\-1&2&-1\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then:

1. $M$ is symmetric positive definite and $K$ is symmetric with
$\ker K=\operatorname{span}\{(1,1,1)\}$;
2. the modal data are as follows, with $M$-orthonormal modal vectors:
   (a) $\lambda_{1}=0$ with $u_{1}=(1,1,1)/\sqrt{2m+M}$: the **translation
   mode**, in which the three labels move together;
   (b) $\lambda_{2}=k/m$ with $u_{2}=(1,0,-1)/\sqrt{2m}$: the
   **antisymmetric stretch**, in which the outer labels move oppositely and
   the middle label is at rest;
   (c) $\lambda_{3}=\frac{k}{m}\bigl(1+\frac{2m}{M}\bigr)$ with
   $u_{3}=(1,-2m/M,1)/\sqrt{2m(1+2m/M)}$: the **symmetric stretch**, in which
   the outer labels move together and the middle label moves oppositely;
3. every motion is
$$q(t)=(a+bt)u_{1}+\bigl(A\cos(\omega_{2}t)+B\sin(\omega_{2}t)\bigr)u_{2}+\bigl(C\cos(\omega_{3}t)+D\sin(\omega_{3}t)\bigr)u_{3}$$
with $\omega_{2}=\sqrt{k/m}$ and $\omega_{3}=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}(1+\frac{2m}{M})}$,
and the pure-zero-mode motions are exactly the affine curves
$q(t)=(a+bt)u_{1}$; for $b\ne0$ they are unbounded on $[0,\infty)$;
4. $\omega_{3}>\omega_{2}$ for all $m,M>0$: in this model the symmetric
stretch is the stiffer vibration.

items.title: The equal-arm double pendulum in the linear approximation: the slow same-side mode, the fast opposite-side mode and the bounded modal motions
items.statement:
Global-time, growth and boundedness claims below refer to the unique maximal extension of the autonomous free equation on $\mathbb R$; local motions remain its restrictions. Values at $0$ in coefficient formulas are evaluated on that extension when the original interval omits $0$.

Let a planar double pendulum consist of two equal particle labels of mass
$m>0$ connected by two equal massless rods of length $l>0$, pivoted at a
fixed point; let $\theta_{1},\theta_{2}$ be the angles of the rods from the
downward vertical, read in radians (dimensionless under the angle convention
of [[def-cm01-units]]), and let $g>0$ be the uniform gravitational
acceleration of the model. In the linear approximation about the downward
equilibrium of the cited treatment, the small-oscillation data are the
coupled quadratic model of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with $n=2$,

$$M=ml^{2}\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad K=mgl\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad J\equiv0 .$$

Write $\gamma_{s}:=2-\sqrt2$, $\gamma_{f}:=2+\sqrt2$. Then:

1. $M$ is symmetric positive definite (with $M^{1/2}$ its unique positive
definite square root) and $K$ is symmetric positive definite, so the model
is oscillatory with both modal stiffnesses positive;
2. the modal data are
$$\lambda_{s}=\frac{g}{l}\gamma_{s}\quad\text{with}\quad w_{s}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\\sqrt2\end{pmatrix},\qquad\lambda_{f}=\frac{g}{l}\gamma_{f}\quad\text{with}\quad w_{f}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-\sqrt2\end{pmatrix},$$
that is $Kw_{s}=\lambda_{s}Mw_{s}$ and $Kw_{f}=\lambda_{f}Mw_{f}$; the
$M$-orthonormal modal vectors are
$u_{s}=w_{s}/\sqrt{2ml^{2}\gamma_{f}}$ and
$u_{f}=w_{f}/\sqrt{2ml^{2}\gamma_{s}}$;
3. the mode frequencies are
$$\omega_{s}=\sqrt{\frac{g}{l}\bigl(2-\sqrt2\bigr)}<\omega_{f}=\sqrt{\frac{g}{l}\bigl(2+\sqrt2\bigr)},$$
and every motion is bounded on $\mathbb R$ and has the form
$$q(t)=\bigl(A\cos(\omega_{s}t)+B\sin(\omega_{s}t)\bigr)u_{s}+\bigl(C\cos(\omega_{f}t)+D\sin(\omega_{f}t)\bigr)u_{f};$$
4. in the slow mode $u_{s}$ the two angles have the same sign
($\theta_{2}=\sqrt2\,\theta_{1}$) and in the fast mode $u_{f}$ they have
opposite signs ($\theta_{2}=-\sqrt2\,\theta_{1}$); the datum
$q(0)=u_{s}$, $q'(0)=0$ excites exactly the slow mode and the datum
$q(0)=u_{f}$, $q'(0)=0$ exactly the fast mode.
items.strategy: Direct: check positive definiteness, verify the two eigenpairs of the equal-arm double pendulum data by explicit multiplication, and read the bounded modal motions and the frequency comparison from the free-mode theorem.

items.title: A doubly degenerate quadratic model: every direction is a mode, the modal basis is not intrinsic, and coupling splits the double frequency
items.statement:
Global-time, growth and boundedness claims below refer to the unique maximal extension of the autonomous free equation on $\mathbb R$; local motions remain its restrictions. Values at $0$ in coefficient formulas are evaluated on that extension when the original interval omits $0$.

Consider two uncoupled oscillators of equal mass and stiffness, modelled by
the coupled quadratic model of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with
$n=2$,

$$M=mI_{2},\qquad K=kI_{2},\qquad J\equiv0,\qquad m>0,\ k>0 .$$

Then:

1. $M$ and $K$ are symmetric positive definite, the matrix
$M^{-1/2}KM^{-1/2}=(k/m)I_{2}$ has the **double** eigenvalue
$\lambda=k/m$, the modal eigenspace is $E_{\lambda}=\mathbb R^{2}$ and
$N_{\lambda}:=\mathbb R^{2}$; every orthonormal basis
$\{e_{1},e_{2}\}$ of $\mathbb R^{2}$ is an orthonormal eigenbasis of that
matrix, so the decoupling data are not unique;
2. every motion is
$$q(t)=\cos(\omega t)\,a+\sin(\omega t)\,b,\qquad a,b\in\mathbb R^{2},\qquad \omega=\sqrt{k/m},$$
and every nonzero vector $a\in\mathbb R^{2}$ spans a pure mode: the datum
$q(0)=a$, $q'(0)=0$ produces the single-frequency oscillation
$q(t)=\cos(\omega t)a$;
3. the frequency $\omega$ and the subspace $N_{\lambda}=\mathbb R^{2}$ are
intrinsic, while individual modal vectors are not: there is no
basis-independent meaning to "the first mode" and no separation of the
motions into two distinguished one-parameter families;
4. **splitting by coupling.** The two-mass model of
[[ex-cm09-two-mass-spring-modes]] with coupling $c>0$ has stiffness
$K_{c}=\begin{pmatrix}k+c&-c\\-c&k+c\end{pmatrix}$, which equals $kI_{2}$ at
$c=0$ and coincides with the data of this example when $c=0$; for $c>0$ its
modal stiffnesses are the **distinct** numbers $k/m$ and $(k+2c)/m$, so an
explicit change of the model data separates the double eigenvalue into the
unchanged in-phase frequency and the raised relative frequency.
items.strategy: Direct: identify the scalar multiple of the identity, read the double eigenvalue and the flexibility of the modal basis, and compare the data with the coupled two-mass instance to exhibit the splitting.
items.physical_scope: A worked instance of degeneracy in the coupled quadratic model: two identical uncoupled oscillators, M = m I, K = k I, with the double modal stiffness k/m, the full two-dimensional eigenspace, the four-parameter family of motions, the non-intrinsic status of every modal basis and the splitting of the double frequency into k/m and (k+2c)/m when a coupling c>0 of the two-mass model is switched on. The parameters are model data; the example asserts no measured frequency and no general stability-of-degeneracy theorem.

items.title: The inverted pendulum about its upward equilibrium: the negative modal stiffness, the exponential quadratic mode and the nonlinear instability
items.statement:
Global-time, growth and boundedness claims below refer to the unique maximal extension of the autonomous free equation on $\mathbb R$; local motions remain its restrictions. Values at $0$ in coefficient formulas are evaluated on that extension when the original interval omits $0$.

Let a planar pendulum consist of one particle label of mass $m>0$ attached
to a fixed pivot by a massless rod of length $l>0$, and let $\theta$ be its
angle from the **upward** vertical, read in radians (dimensionless under
[[def-cm01-units]]); let $g>0$ be the uniform gravitational acceleration of
the model. In the chart with kinetic metric field $M(\theta)=ml^{2}$ and
potential $U(\theta)=mgl\cos\theta$, the mechanical system of
[[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]] has energy
$E=\tfrac12ml^{2}\theta'^{2}+mgl\cos\theta$ and equation
$ml^{2}\theta''=mgl\sin\theta$, that is $\theta''=(g/l)\sin\theta$. Then:

1. $\theta=0$ is a mechanical equilibrium and a strict local **maximum** of
$U$ on the chart, with $K:=D^{2}U(0)=-mgl<0$; the small-oscillation model
of clause (d) of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] is the one-dimensional
quadratic model $ml^{2}\xi''-mgl\,\xi=0$, whose modal stiffness is
$\lambda=-g/l<0$;
2. with $\kappa:=\sqrt{g/l}>0$ every motion of that quadratic model on an
interval with nonempty interior is
$$\xi(t)=a\cosh(\kappa t)+b\sinh(\kappa t),\qquad a,b\in\mathbb R,$$
and the datum $\xi(0)=0$, $\xi'(0)=b\ne0$ gives
$\xi(t)=(b/\kappa)\sinh(\kappa t)$, unbounded on $[0,\infty)$;
3. the rest point of the quadratic model is not Lyapunov stable
([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]): with
$\varepsilon_{0}=1$ and every $\delta>0$, a datum of size
$<\delta$ leads to a motion reaching norm $1$;
4. the **nonlinear** upward equilibrium $(\theta,\theta')=(0,0)$ of the
pendulum chart system is not Lyapunov stable either: the field
$F(\theta,v)=(v,(g/l)\sin\theta)$ is $C^{1}$ with $F(0,0)=0$ and
$DF(0,0)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\ g/l&0\end{pmatrix}$, whose eigenvalues
$\pm\sqrt{g/l}$ are real, nonzero and include the positive value
$\sqrt{g/l}$, so the hyperbolic-saddle theorem applies.
items.strategy: Direct: read the negative stiffness of the inverted pendulum from its chart potential, solve the repulsive scalar equation, and apply the free-mode instability clause and the hyperbolic-saddle theorem.
items.physical_scope: A worked instance of an unstable quadratic direction: the planar inverted pendulum of mass m and length l about its upward equilibrium, with chart data M = m l^2 and U(theta) = m g l cos(theta) measured from the upward vertical, negative Hessian -m g l, the exact exponential motions of the small-oscillation model and the exponential escaping family of the quadratic model, together with the nonlinear Lyapunov instability of the upward equilibrium obtained from the hyperbolic-saddle theorem. The example is a conditional statement about the declared mathematical model; g, m and l are model parameters and no measured period or escape time is asserted.

items.title: A drive along the in-phase pattern of the two-mass chain: resonance exactly at that mode's frequency and a bounded steady response off resonance
items.statement:
Adopt the two-mass chain of [[ex-cm09-two-mass-spring-modes]]: mass metric
$M=mI_{2}$, stiffness $K=\begin{pmatrix}k+c&-c\\-c&k+c\end{pmatrix}$ with
$m>0$, $k>0$, $c>0$, and modal vectors $u_{\pm}=(1,\pm1)/\sqrt{2m}$ with
modal stiffnesses $\lambda_{+}=k/m$, $\lambda_{-}=(k+2c)/m$ and frequencies
$\omega_{+}=\sqrt{k/m}$, $\omega_{-}=\sqrt{(k+2c)/m}$. Choose a real drive
amplitude $F\ne0$ and a frequency $\Omega\ge0$, and adopt the prescribed
sinusoidal generalized force in the modelling status of
[[post-cm04-sinusoidal-drive-model]]:

$$J(t)=F\cos(\Omega t)\,u_{+},$$

so the model is the forced coupled quadratic model $Mq''+Kq=J$. The all-time claims below concern maximal motions on $\mathbb R$; local solutions are their restrictions. Then:

1. the modal force components of $J(t)=J_{0}\cos(\Omega t)$ with
$J_{0}=Fu_{+}$ are $\psi_{0}=O^{\mathsf T}M^{-1/2}J_{0}=(F/m,\,0)$: the
drive excites the in-phase modal coordinate alone, with modal amplitude
$F/m$, and leaves the relative coordinate unforced;
2. if $\Omega=\omega_{+}=\sqrt{k/m}$, then
$$q^{\mathrm{p}}(t)=\frac{F}{2m\omega_{+}}\,t\sin(\omega_{+}t)\,u_{+}$$
is a motion of the model, of in-phase pattern, with linearly growing
amplitude $|F|t/(2m\omega_{+})$, and **every** motion of the model is
unbounded on $[0,\infty)$;
3. if $\Omega^{2}\ne k/m$ then every motion of the model is bounded on
$[0,\infty)$; in particular at $\Omega=\omega_{-}=\sqrt{(k+2c)/m}$ — the
frequency of the *unforced* relative mode — the drive is non-resonant and
the steady response has amplitude
$$\frac{\lvert F\rvert/m}{\lvert k/m-(k+2c)/m\rvert}=\frac{\lvert F\rvert}{2c};$$
4. the resonance condition is exactly that the drive frequency equal the
frequency of a mode whose modal force component does not vanish: here the
in-phase mode at $\omega_{+}$, not the relative mode at $\omega_{-}$.
items.strategy: Direct: compute the modal force of the in-phase drive, instantiate the resonant and non-resonant cases of the forced modal theorem, and evaluate the steady amplitude at the relative-mode frequency.
items.physical_scope: A worked instance of the forced coupled quadratic model: the two equal-mass chain of the companion example with a prescribed sinusoidal generalized force J(t)=F cos(Omega t) u_+ along the in-phase pattern, the modal force components (F/m,0), the unbounded resonance at Omega = sqrt(k/m) with the explicit linearly growing modal motion, the bounded steady response of amplitude |F|/(2c) at Omega = sqrt((k+2c)/m), and the boundedness of every motion for Omega^2 not equal to k/m. The drive is prescribed external data; no back-reaction, measured response or empirical value is asserted.

items.title: An explicit weakly damped oscillator: the averaging constants and the energy-decay bound on five thousand oscillation periods
items.statement:
Adopt the damped oscillator model of [[post-cm04-linear-damping-model]] with
data

$$m=1\ \text{kg},\qquad k=1\ \text{kg/s}^{2},\qquad \varepsilon=10^{-4},\qquad \gamma=1\ \text{kg/s},$$

so that $c=\varepsilon\gamma=10^{-4}$ kg/s and $\omega_{0}=\sqrt{k/m}=1$
rad/s; the angles and frequencies are read under the convention of
[[def-cm01-units]]. Take the initial rotating-frame amplitude
$\zeta_{0}=1$, the ball data $R=1/2$, $\rho=1/4$ and the horizon parameter
$A=1/2$. Then:

1. the averaging data of [[pthm-cm09-averaging-for-weak-damping]] specialize
to $P=2\pi$, $F(t,\zeta)=-ie^{it}(\cos t\operatorname{Im}\zeta-\sin t\operatorname{Re}\zeta)$
and $\bar F(\zeta)=-\zeta/2$, with averaged solution
$\bar\zeta(t)=e^{-\varepsilon t/2}=e^{-t/(2\cdot10^{4})}$;
2. the constants of the averaging estimate are
$$M=\frac{3\sqrt2}{2},\qquad L=\sqrt2,\qquad B=6\sqrt2\,\pi,\qquad B_{1}=4\sqrt2\,\pi,\qquad K=2\pi\bigl(3\sqrt2+6\bigr)e^{\sqrt2/2},$$
so that
$$K\approx1.30522\times10^{2},\qquad \varepsilon K\approx1.30522\times10^{-2}<0.25=\rho;$$
3. the trapping hypothesis holds:
$\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert(1-e^{-\gamma A/(2m)})=1-e^{-1/4}\approx0.22120< R-\rho=0.25$,
and also $1/4=\gamma A/(2m)\le\ln(4/3)\approx0.28768$;
4. consequently the motion with datum $x(0)=\sqrt2$ m, $x'(0)=0$ — which
has $\zeta(0)=1$ and mechanical energy $E_{0}=m\omega_{0}\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert^{2}=1$ J —
satisfies
$$\bigl\lvert E(t)-e^{-t/10^{4}}\bigr\rvert\le m\omega_{0}\varepsilon K\bigl(2\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert+\varepsilon K\bigr)\approx2.62748\times10^{-2}\ \text{J}\qquad(0\le t\le5000),$$
the interval $[0,5000]$ being $[0,A/\varepsilon]$ and containing
$5000/(2\pi)\approx795.8$ oscillation periods of the undamped frequency;
5. at the end of the horizon the averaged energy is
$e^{-1/2}\approx0.60653$ J, so the estimate bounds the deviation of the
exact energy from the averaged exponential decay by about $4.3\%$ of its
value there.
items.strategy: Direct: specialize the averaging theorem data, evaluate the exact constants, check the smallness and trapping hypotheses and state the energy-decay bound with its decimal values.
items.physical_scope: A worked numerical instance of the weak-damping averaging estimate: the model m x'' + epsilon gamma x' + k x = 0 with m = 1 kg, k = 1 kg/s^2, epsilon = 10^-4 and gamma = 1 kg/s, initial rotating-frame amplitude zeta_0 = 1, ball radii R = 1/2 and rho = 1/4 and horizon parameter A = 1/2, verifying the smallness and trapping hypotheses with the exact constants M = 3 sqrt2/2, L = sqrt2, K = 2 pi (3 sqrt2 + 6) exp(sqrt2/2) and concluding that the mechanical energy tracks the averaged exponential exp(-t/10^4) within 2.63 x 10^-2 on the interval [0,5000]. The numbers are exact-arithmetic evaluations of the model formulas, not measurements; no apparatus, no observed decay and no empirical statement is present.
